findings.title: Expand home paths before passing them to the Python smoke runner
findings.trigger: An executor follows the modified smoke-run recipe and uses the stated ~/triggarr value as subprocess cwd.
findings.execution_path: Task 3 step 2 adapts run_smoke.py using a Python argv list and cwd. Unlike shell command arguments, subprocess cwd does not undergo tilde expansion. The launch fails before Claude starts; step 3 then requires recording INCOMPLETE and stopping.
findings.consequence: Re-executing this plan cannot complete its positive smoke verification without an undocumented correction. The --add-dir argv value has the same missing explicit expansion.
findings.evidence: The diff replaces the previous absolute cwd with ~/triggarr. A direct subprocess reproduction raised FileNotFoundError naming '~/triggarr'. Neither this instruction nor the searched research text specifies expanduser for these Python arguments. The pytest evidence does not exercise this executor recipe.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep paths portable by explicitly constructing cwd and --add-dir with Path.home() or Path(...).expanduser(), and stringify the expanded paths when building argv.

limitations: Did not independently run pytest in the read-only sandbox; used the harness-produced evidence for the exact inspected head.
Did not execute the publication gate or its self-test because they create temporary directories and repositories. Both scripts received syntax/static review.
Did not independently query live GitHub settings or external services; reviewed the repository's policy statements and implementation.
The finding reproduces the Python launch failure, not the complete external Claude smoke workflow.
